newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Texaco realigns units.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Texaco realigns units.

text.p: Texaco Inc said it would realign its operations along business lines and consolidate worldwide exploration and production and international refining and marketing. The company also announced a series of management changes.
A full text of the company's announcement follows.
---PRESS RELEASE----------------------------------- Texaco Announces Companywide Realignment Designed To Increase Efficiency And Improve Performance
Business Editors
WHITE PLAINS, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct. 30, 1996--
New Units Aligned According to Business Lines

Citing the goal of enhancing its ability to grow existing and new businesses in the sharply competitive global petroleum industry, Texaco Inc. today announced a companywide organizational realignment effective January 1, 1997.

Under the new structure, the company will be organized along business lines, consolidating such units as worldwide exploration and production as well as international refining and marketing operations. Texaco also is creating New Business Development units to provide greater focus on global growth opportunities. In addition, the company is establishing senior-level Leadership Councils to provide strategic direction and coordination in key business areas.

All of these efforts will be led by a strong new leadership team that combines individuals with long experience in operations with others who bring fresh perspectives to new challenges and responsibilities.

According to Texaco Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Peter I. Bijur, "The petroleum business today is global and intensely competitive. To succeed in this environment, and build on our current performance, we must be able to grow our existing businesses, and identify, analyze and execute on new opportunities more swiftly. That demands that we move faster, communicate better and coordinate more closely, so that we can maximize our overall performance, profitability and growth prospects in chosen markets.

"By placing groups which perform similar work in the same location," Bijur added, "they will be able to share information, ideas and resources more readily -- and to move critical information throughout the organization more directly and openly.
"We are giving a new team of energetic Texaco managers the authority to execute our agenda for growth. All share a commitment to long-term growth, and are responsible for achieving results."

Bijur emphasized the New Business Development groups as a key new element of Texaco's organization. "Creation of New Business Development units will help us identify and develop opportunities and new revenue sources more quickly, as well as help guide projects more efficiently toward realization.

"Our Leadership Councils will be the central means of setting strategy, policy and coordinating our activities across business lines and throughout the company. The Councils will help to make Texaco function as a seamless organization."

Bijur also noted that the realignment affects reporting and management functions, not ongoing field operations. While some overlapping activities may be eliminated, the new structure is designed to stimulate growth rather than simply cut costs. Business Units -- Growth Creation and Cost Containment
Under the new Texaco organizational structure announced today:

Worldwide Upstream functions will be directed by C. Robert Black, 61, Senior Vice President of Texaco Inc., who will be named President of Texaco Worldwide Exploration and Production. As a member of the senior executive team, Black will be located in Harrison, N.Y. The four upstream operating units will be based in Houston and will be composed of the following:
Worldwide Exploration, with Bruce S. Appelbaum, 49, currently President of Texaco's International Exploration Division, to be named President of Texaco Exploration;

International Producing, to be headed by Robert A. Solberg, 50, currently Vice President of Texaco Inc. and President of Texaco's Middle East/Far East Division. Solberg will be named President of Texaco International Production;

North American Producing will be led by Claire S. Farley, 37, currently Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Hydro-Texaco Holdings. Farley will be named President of Texaco North America Production and has been elected a Vice President of Texaco Inc. effective January 1, 1997; and

New Business Development, which will be headed by Thomas L. Hazen, 52, now President and Chief Executive Officer of the Timan Pechora Company. Hazen will be named Vice President of Texaco Exploration and Production New Business Development.

International Downstream activities will be based in Harrison, N.Y., and headed by Clarence P. Cazalot, Jr., 45, currently Vice President of Texaco Inc. and President of Texaco Exploration and Production Inc. Cazalot will be named President of Texaco International Marketing and Manufacturing. The unit is composed of the following:

Marketing, to be headed by Eugene Celentano, 58, Vice President of Texaco Inc. and currently President of Texaco's Latin America/West Africa Division. Celentano will be named President of Texaco International Marketing;
Manufacturing, which will be led by Wayne N. Clark, 51, now General Manager of Texaco's Pembroke Wales plant; Clark will be named Vice President of Texaco International Manufacturing; and

New Business Development will report to John E. Bethancourt, 45, now Managing Director - Business Development in Texaco's Middle East/Far East Division. He will be named Vice President of Texaco International Business Development. Global Businesses -- Coordinating Texaco's Worldwide Presence

The company also announced a unit to coordinate those Texaco operations, including two new global business units, which will benefit from special emphasis and attention. The Global Businesses unit will be based in Harrison, N.Y., and will be led by Glenn F. Tilton, 48, Senior Vice President of Texaco Inc. and currently President of Texaco USA, who will be named President of Global Businesses. The unit will include the following:
Oversight responsibility for Texaco's interest in the Caltex Petroleum Company, Texaco's downstream joint venture with Chevron;

While discussions continue with Shell and Star Enterprise about a possible downstream U.S. alliance, the Texaco U.S. Downstream and oversight of Star Enterprise, Texaco's joint venture with Saudi Refining Inc., will be included in this unit;

Worldwide Gas and Power, a new unit to be headed by Thomas M. Matthews, 53, Vice President of Texaco Inc. and Vice President of Texaco Natural Gas Inc., which also will include the former Alternate Energy Division;
Worldwide Lubricants, a new unit to direct the efforts of Texaco and affiliate units worldwide in the lubricants business. A leader of this unit will be named in the near future;
The worldwide operations of Texaco Fuel and Marine Marketing and International Aviation Sales; and

Technology, which will include the units dedicated to both upstream and downstream businesses, as well as the Information Technology Department. This unit will be headed by Ronald J. Robinson, 50, now President of Texaco's Technology Division. Corporate -- Aligning Financial Functions with Businesses

In Harrison, Patrick J. Lynch, 58, currently Vice President of Texaco Inc. and President of Texaco Europe, will become Texaco's new Chief Financial Officer. In addition to responsibility for the Comptrollers, Investor Relations and Shareholder Services, Risk Management, Tax and Finance functions, the office of the CFO will have responsibility for Corporate Planning and Economics and Oil Trading and Transport.

Allen J. Krowe, 64, will continue as Vice Chairman of Texaco. Senior Vice President Stephen M. Turner, 57, remains as General Counsel, and Corporate Communications will continue to be led by Senior Vice President William K. Tell, Jr., 62. Corporate Secretary Carl B. Davidson, 63, and President of the Human Resources Division Richard F. Brenner, 56, will remain in their current posts.
William C. Bousquette, 60, the company's current Chief Financial Officer, has elected to retire at the end of 1996. Leadership Councils -- Strategic Linkages for Sustained Growth

The company also announced a coordinating network of Leadership Councils, composed of employees from different levels of management across the company, which are designed to share information, facilitate decisions, allocate resources and monitor progress across business lines. Leadership Councils will be organized in the following areas:

An Executive Council, chaired by Peter I. Bijur, charged with setting strategy and ensuring execution of agreed priorities. Other members of the council include Allen J. Krowe, C. Robert Black, Patrick J. Lynch, Glenn F. Tilton, Clarence P. Cazalot and James R. Metzger, head of Corporate Planning and Economics;

A Growth Council, which will coordinate Texaco's approach to seeking new business opportunities across the breadth of the organization. It also will manage growth processes, making best practices systematic and repeatable throughout the company;
A Management Development Council, to be led by Richard F. Brenner, which will set standards for recruiting, training and development, and succession planning;
The Technology Council, which will be headed by Ronald J. Robinson, and will maintain and build the company's leading position in technology throughout its operations; and
The Operations Council, which will be the chief vehicle for information sharing on key operational issues across organizations and functions. Peter I. Bijur will direct the Operations Council.
In summary, Bijur said, "Our new structure and the strong new leadership team will help us achieve our primary goal of building a stronger Texaco for the 21st century." -0-
